data.name: Amitray
data.gender_notes: Amitray is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words 'amita' meaning infinite, and 'asurya' meaning immortal. The name Amitray carries the meaning “Boundless Immortality” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amitray usually hope their child will grow to embody boundless immortality and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizing eternal life and boundless wisdom.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amitray total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Amitray" signifies boundless wealth and prosperity, as well as a person with infinite generosity and kindness. It reflects the virtues of hospitality, giving, and charitable nature deeply embedded in the Hindu culture. One who bears this name is believed to bring good fortune, and is often associated with being a benevolent and righteous leader, inspiring respect and loyalty.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Amitray" represents a connection to the divine source of all existence, where the infinite and immortal aspect symbolizes the ultimate reality of the soul beyond the physical realm. It underscores the notion of spiritual wealth and underscores the importance of selfless giving, kindness, and continuous spiritual growth. Wearing this name inspire one to embody the virtues of compassion, love, and pursuit of spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Amitray: Radiating infinite love and peace. The embodiment of compassion and grace.

vedic_reference.note: From Vedic literature, Amitra means 'friend' and Āya is a suffix indicating respect. Together, Amitray means 'Friend of the Immortals'.

historical_references.reference: Amitraya or Amitra was a prominent Jaina monk and theologian during the 5th century BCE. He was a leading figure in the Shvetambara Jaina tradition and is known for his works on Jaina scriptures and philosophy.

Amitrayus or Amitraghata was a king mentioned in the Tibetan Book of the Dead (Bardo Thodol). He is described as a just ruler, who brought peace and prosperity to his kingdom before his death, and who is believed to assist the deceased in the bardo (intermediate state) between death and rebirth.

Amitray is seen as a symbol of selflessness and compassion, and can be a source of inspiration for individuals seeking personal growth and mindfulness.
